description: §7.6 rule (b) (S482) — `${ const a = note("a"); }` written in an element inside the `Idle` arm of a `<match>`: the initializer calls a function, and a file-scope initializer runs once — not when, or each time, the arm shows — so it is refused, naming the arm (E-FILE-SCOPE-INIT-IN-CONSTRUCT). Before #2053 r1 it ran once, unconditionally, with the `Ready` arm showing.
rationale: §7.6 rule (b) (S482): "Inside the content of an `if=` / `else-if=` / `else` element, a component's slot content, or a `<match>` arm, at any depth … A file-scope initializer written there that acts — a call, a write, a `?{}` query, a foreign block — SHALL be a compile error, `E-FILE-SCOPE-INIT-IN-CONSTRUCT`, whose message names the construct." ruling:user-voice-scrml.md-S481-nested-init-chain-comments item 1 — "A file-scope initializer that acts, written inside `if=` content, a component's slot content, or a `<match>` … make it a compile error naming the construct; refusing means nobody is surprised." (owner: "aprove both, lets wrap").
